findings.reason: the plan must specify how a rendered prompt name binds to a response model (cross-function/cross-module resolution or an explicit call-site registry) or the test it proposes cannot be written as described.
findings.text: the AST-pinning test's stated premise that "each [call site] renders a prompt by name and passes response_model= to call_llm_structured" is false in the code: the render and the response_model argument live in different scopes and even different modules (imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:256 renders "code/triage" while imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:298 passes response_model=FileTriageBatch; imas_codex/discovery/paths/scorer.py:282 renders "paths/triage" in _build_system_prompt while imas_codex/discovery/paths/scorer.py:143 passes response_model=TriageBatch in triage_batch); the plan gives no association rule, so the walker cannot pair prompt to model and its positive control cannot reach twelve

findings.reason: the plan's expected prompt set and the positive-control assertion must be corrected to the prompts that actually have a call site, or the fail-closed control fails on a plan defect rather than a walker defect.
findings.text: two of the twelve prompts the plan lists as discovery call-site prompts are never rendered anywhere in imas_codex/ (no render_prompt call site for "signals/individualization" or "discovery/enricher"; the only occurrences of individualization are a log string at imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:4397), so the plan's "every prompt rendered by a discovery call site" set and its twelve-prompt positive control include prompts no call site renders

findings.reason: the mechanism is landed and does centralize the clause; only the plan's description of parameter-name ownership is inaccurate, so correcting the text does not change the implemented design.
findings.text: §14 states render_path_prefix_clause owns the query parameter name inside the function and that callers "stop hand-wiring the clause and its parameter name", but the landed signature is render_path_prefix_clause(alias: str, param: str) and callers still supply the name ("root_filter" at imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:484, "path_prefixes" at imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:98)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — both §22 changes land inside existing deep modules (the structured-call loop in imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py and the schema binding in imas_codex/llm/prompt_loader.py) behind interfaces that do not grow; the local change removes a request field rather than adding surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's §14 account claims render_path_prefix_clause owns the query parameter name inside the function, but the landed signature still takes it from each caller.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §14 and §22 add no CLI option, MCP view, public definition or error family (the plan states the abort case adds none), and §22 retires _DEFAULT_SCHEMA_NEEDS, so nothing is added that needs to be retired or merged.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites real existing machinery (EmptyResponseError, RETRYABLE_PATTERNS, _local_call_kwargs, schema_needs, _SCHEMA_PROVIDERS, _DEFAULT_SCHEMA_NEEDS) but asserts a call-site shape it never opened, and two of the twelve prompts its new test names have no call site at all.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no new wrapper is proposed; `_local_call_kwargs` is edited in place and no parallel layer is added.
